note: authserver.json - the login program's settings in this flavor (docs/decisions/0016-a-server-is-a-flavor.md). Reference: src/server/apps/authserver/authserver.conf.dist, whose setting names these are; the format is this project's (docs/decisions/0005-json-configuration.md). This file is part of the flavor and is shared with it, so it holds nothing one machine alone knows: the database logins, the addresses and ports the program binds, and the paths of the machine's own files are in config/machine.json, section authserver, and a key stated there wins over this file. A path that names this flavor's own content is relative to this folder. Only the settings the ported stages read are here - a setting arrives with the stage that reads it, so a key in this file is one the program actually uses.

CreationMap.doc: The map id that means the character-creation instance. A client naming it as a place - which this client does when a character is clicked, 0x8029 with map 0 and type 0 - is placed where the character's row says instead (game/src/Maps/Placement.rs). 0 is the creation instance's own id in the world's catalogue.

FallbackOutpost.doc: Where a character whose row names no map and which has never been in an outpost enters. A setting rather than a rule: the outpost a character starts in is written by creation and by travelling, never derived, and this program holds no map catalogue to pick one from (docs/port/04-configuration.md).

EquippedBag.doc: The id of the bag a character wears things in. The login's character list draws each character's armour from the items in this bag (slots 2 to 6: body, legs, head, boots, gloves). It must be the bag the world's creation inventory gives type 2 and model 21 (config/flavors/Vanilla/World/creation/inventory.json); a different number lists every character with no armour.

StatusInterval.doc: How often the program writes its own status line, in seconds: how long it has been up, where it listens, and how many connections it has accepted. A server that cannot say whether anything reached it cannot be tested.

EffectiveConfig.doc: Every key this program read from this file, with any database password masked, at debug. It needs its logger: Logger.server.loading = 6,Console Auth.

Enable.doc: The portal the client takes its identity from before it logs in: four HTTP endpoints. This program serves it (docs/decisions/0003-portal-host.md), and the accounts it answers from are data/accounts.json. Where it answers is the machine's (config/machine.json, authserver.Portal.Bind).

The link Kryta.dll opens from inside a patched client when the client starts (docs/port/22-client-platform.md). This program serves it: over it a client is given the offsets its DLL finds the client's functions by, and the custom title text. A patched client does not start without it. Where it answers is the machine's (config/machine.json, authserver.ClientLink.Bind).

Directory.doc: The folder of what a client's DLL is given, relative to this flavor's folder: every *.json under its offsets folder is one offset document (Client/README.md). Read once at start-up; a missing folder or a broken file stops the program.

TitleWorldConfig.doc: The world program's settings file, relative to this flavor's folder. Its WorldPack supplies the custom title text and the map files a client's DLL is sent. An empty value sends none.

MapPartPauseMs.doc: Milliseconds the server waits before each 256 KiB part of a map file it sends to a client (docs/port/24-custom-maps.md, D8). 0 sends at full speed, which is what a server in use wants. A value above 0 stands in for a slow link or a very large map, to try a map load that has to wait for its file: a 2.9 MB map is 12 parts, so 5000 makes it take a minute.

Threads.doc: Threads serving the accepted sockets, for both listeners this program opens. Reference: Network.Threads, whose default is this. Must be greater than 0; a connection goes to the thread with the fewest already.

Trace.doc: Every byte of every connection, in and out, as a debug line. Off by default in a served server: it is an instrument for an investigation. It needs its logger: Logger.network.trace = 6,Console Auth.
Every statement the database layer runs, as a debug line. It needs its logger: Logger.sql.trace = 6,Console Auth.

RealmsStateUpdateDelay.doc: How often the world list is refreshed, in seconds. Reference: RealmsStateUpdateDelay, whose default is this.

WorkerThreads.doc: Asynchronous connections to the login database.

SynchThreads.doc: Synchronous connections, used where the caller cannot wait for a callback.

WorkerThreads.doc: Asynchronous connections to the character database.

Console.doc: Type, level, flags, then the type's own fields. Type 1 is the console and its last field is the colour list for fatal, error, warn, info, debug, trace. The levels are 1 fatal to 6 trace; 4 is info. A line about one connection is written at debug, so this level shows the login program's own state and its problems, not its traffic.

Auth.doc: Type 2 is a file: the name, then the mode (a append, w overwrite).

root.doc: Level, then appender names. A logger inherits from its dotted parent and finally from root.

network.trace.doc: The byte trace's own logger. Its level is what decides whether Network.Trace shows anything: 6 is trace, which is where the bytes are written.

sql.trace.doc: The database trace's own logger, read the same way.

auth.trace.doc: The decrypted body of each message the client sends, which the byte trace cannot show: it holds the ciphertext, and the key is per connection.

server.loading.doc: The effective configuration dump, and the loading stages.
